stops.title: Thermal equilibrium & Zeroth law
stops.inShort: Two systems in thermal equilibrium have the same temperature. Zeroth law: if A and B are separately in thermal equilibrium with C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

stops.title: Heat, internal energy & First law of thermodynamics
stops.inShort: First law of thermodynamics is conservation of energy: Q = ΔU + W, where W = ∫ P dV is work done by the system. Positive Q means heat added; positive W means expansion.

stops.title: Thermodynamic state variables & p-V diagram
stops.inShort: Intensive variables (P, T, ρ) are independent of system size; extensive variables (V, M, U) depend on mass/size. Area under the p-V curve gives work done W = ∫ P dV.

stops.title: Thermodynamic processes (isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, isochoric)
stops.inShort: Isothermal (T const): W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁). Isobaric (P const): W = P(V₂−V₁). Isochoric (V const): W = 0, Q = ΔU. Adiabatic (Q = 0): PV^γ = const, W = (P₁V₁ − P₂V₂)/(γ−1).

stops.title: Heat engines, refrigerators & Second law
stops.inShort: Heat engine efficiency η = W/Q_H = 1 − Q_C/Q_H. Refrigerator COP K = Q_C/W = Q_C/(Q_H − Q_C). Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the Second Law are equivalent.

stops.title: Carnot cycle & Carnot engine
stops.inShort: Carnot cycle consists of two isothermal and two adiabatic reversible processes. Maximum efficiency η_max = 1 − T_C/T_H depends only on reservoir temperatures.

items.s: Q: heat supplied; ΔU: change in internal energy; W: work done by system.

items.f: W = n R T ln(V₂/V₁) = 2.303 n R T log₁₀(V₂/V₁)
items.s: ΔU = 0 for ideal gas in isothermal process, so Q = W.

items.f: P V^γ = const,  W = (P₁V₁ − P₂V₂)/(γ − 1) = nR(T₁ − T₂)/(γ − 1)
items.s: Q = 0; adiabatic curve is steeper than isothermal by factor γ.
Temperatures T_C and T_H must be in Kelvin.

board.text: "If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are also in thermal equilibrium with each other." This statement refers to ____.

points.text: Correct option: (a) zeroth law of thermodynamics

board.text: What do you mean by a thermodynamic system?
board.answer: A thermodynamic system is a collection or a quantity of matter enclosed within a well-defined boundary, separated from its surroundings, whose state can be described by macroscopic variables (P, V, T).

points.text: Clear definition of thermodynamic system and boundary

board.text: A gas of 0.5 mole at 300 K expands isothermally from an initial volume of 2.0 litre to a final volume of 6.0 litre. What is the work done by gas? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

points.text: Formula W = 2.303 nRT log₁₀(V₂/V₁) and substitution

board.text: In a thermodynamic system, define: (a) Mechanical equilibrium (b) Chemical equilibrium and (c) Thermal equilibrium.
board.answer:
(a) Mechanical equilibrium: There are no unbalanced forces within the system or between the system and its surroundings (pressure is uniform throughout).
(b) Chemical equilibrium: There are no net chemical reactions or transfer of matter from one part of the system to another.
(c) Thermal equilibrium: The temperature of the system is uniform throughout and does not change with time.

points.text: Definition of mechanical equilibrium (no unbalanced forces / uniform P)
Definition of chemical equilibrium (no net chemical reaction)
Definition of thermal equilibrium (uniform constant temperature)

board.text: An ideal mono-atomic gas is adiabatically compressed so that its final temperature is twice its initial temperature. Calculate the ratio of final pressure to its initial pressure.
board.answer:
For adiabatic process: T^γ P^(1−γ) = constant ⇒ P₂/P₁ = (T₂/T₁)^(γ/(γ−1)).
For monoatomic gas, γ = 5/3 ⇒ γ/(γ−1) = (5/3)/(2/3) = 5/2 = 2.5.
Given T₂/T₁ = 2.
P₂/P₁ = 2^(2.5) = 4√2 ≈ 5.657.

points.text: Adiabatic P-T relation P₂/P₁ = (T₂/T₁)^(γ/(γ−1)) with γ = 5/3

board.text: Derive an expression for work done during an isothermal process.
board.answer:
In an isothermal process, temperature T = constant and PV = nRT.
Small work done dW = P dV = (nRT/V) dV.
Integrating from V₁ to V₂:
W = ∫(V₁ to V₂) (nRT/V) dV = nRT [ln V](V₁ to V₂) = nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = 2.303 nRT log₁₀(V₂/V₁).

points.text: dW = P dV and P = nRT/V
